D: Bilbo Baggins is swept off on a quest with thirteen dwarves to reclaim their mountain home.
P: Serve the snacks when the dwarves raid Bilbo's pantry.
S: the dwarves clearing out Bilbo's pantry
Aged cheddar, pork pie, pickled onions, apples and crusty bread piled onto a big board for everyone to grab.
the dwarves turning up their noses at elvish greens in Rivendell
Baby leaves, pea shoots, cucumber and herbs dressed with lemon and olive oil, scattered with toasted seeds.
Gollum and the riddles in the dark
Flathead pieces dusted in seasoned flour, fried in hot oil until crisp, served with tartare sauce and lemon wedges.
M: the three trolls roasting mutton over the fire
Lamb leg rubbed with garlic, rosemary and salt, roasted at 180C for 90 minutes, with roast potatoes and carrots.
Bilbo's love of a proper meal
Pork sausages, bacon, mushrooms and halved tomatoes fried in one pan, eggs fried in the fat, served with buttered toast.
W: the seed cake the dwarves eat at Bag End
Butter cake with caraway seeds baked in a loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes, sliced and served with tea.
K: the dwarves' rowdy feast at Bag End
Cold brown ale in big mugs, or ginger beer for the hobbits who don't drink.

s.note: the dwarves clearing out Bilbo's pantry
s.how: Pile wedges of aged cheddar, sliced pork pies, a jar of pickled onions, apple wedges and torn crusty bread onto a big board. Set it out so a dozen unexpected guests can raid it at once.

s.note: the dwarves turning up their noses at elvish greens in Rivendell
s.how: Toss mixed salad leaves with pea shoots, thinly sliced cucumber and torn mint. Dress with lemon juice and olive oil and scatter with toasted pepitas. Pile it lightly onto a pale platter, as elegant as an Elvish table.

m.note: Bilbo's love of a proper meal
m.how: Fry 8 thick pork sausages until browned. Add 8 rashers bacon, 200g sliced mushrooms and halved tomatoes to the pan. Fry 4 eggs in the fat at the end. Serve with buttered toast, because this is the second breakfast of the day.

w.note: the seed cake the dwarves eat at Bag End
w.how: Beat 175g butter with 175g sugar, then beat in 3 eggs. Fold in 225g self-raising flour, 2 tsp caraway seeds and a splash of milk. Bake in a lined loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes. Cool and slice to serve with a cup of tea.

d.note: the dwarves' rowdy feast at Bag End
d.how: Chill brown ale and pour into big heavy mugs, letting it foam over the top. For anyone not drinking, pour ginger beer into the same mugs. Bang them on the table and sing as loud as you like.
